learning_objective: 📈 Learn how economists measure inflation, track the cost of living, and compare the value of money across different years!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: सूचकांक (समय या स्थान के साथ चरों में सापेक्ष परिवर्तन की माप)
आधार वर्ष (तुलना के लिए चुना गया संदर्भ वर्ष, जिसका मान 100 माना जाता है)
चालू वर्ष (वह वर्ष जिसके लिए सूचकांक निकाला जा रहा है)
मुद्रास्फीति / महंगाई (समय के साथ कीमतों में सामान्य वृद्धि)
उपभोक्ता मूल्य सूचकांक (आम उपभोक्ता द्वारा खरीदी जाने वाली वस्तुओं की कीमतों का सूचकांक)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is a statistical device that measures the relative change in the level of a variable (like prices, production, or stock market) over time compared to a fixed point in the past.

The Base Year is the normal, stable year used for comparison. Its index is always assumed to be 100. The Current Year is the year we are investigating. If the current year index is 120, it means prices have risen by 20% since the base year.

There are Unweighted indices (where all items are treated equally, like Simple Aggregative: P01 = ΣP1/ΣP0 × 100) and Weighted indices (where important items like 'wheat' get more weight than 'salt' based on consumption).

Also known as the Cost of Living Index. It measures changes in the retail prices of a specific basket of goods and services used by average households. It is used by the government to calculate Dearness Allowance (DA) for employees.

It tracks the prices of goods traded in bulk (wholesale level) before they reach the consumer. It includes primary articles, fuel, and manufactured goods. It is a key indicator of widespread inflation in the economy.

fun_activity.title: 🎈 The Shrinking Rupee
fun_activity.instructions: Ask your grandparents how much a cup of tea or a movie ticket cost when they were your age. Compare it to today's price. The product hasn't changed, but the purchasing power of money has fallen. Index numbers mathematically track this 'shrinking value' of money!

exam_tips: 📌 P01 represents the Price Index of the current year (1) with respect to the base year (0).
📌 Always ensure the Base Year chosen is a 'normal' year—free from wars, famines, or extreme economic crises.
📌 The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) does NOT include services (like haircuts or doctor visits), whereas the Consumer Price Index (CPI) includes both goods and services.
quick_recap: ⭐ Index numbers are often called 'Economic Barometers' because they measure the atmospheric pressure of the economy.
⭐ The Sensex and Nifty are famous index numbers that track the performance of the Indian stock market.
⭐ Index numbers deal with relative changes (percentages), not absolute changes.
